raw: | A mapping rooted at a **nested schema element** cannot be authored, and `describe` prints it as if it were rooted at the document root — output that PARSES and executes, producing a mapping whose members do not exist at that level | Studio Pro lets the author start a mapping at any element and stores that as the root element's `JsonPath`; 13 of the 327 demo-app documents do (`OpenAI_API.IM_OpenAI` at `(Object)\|choices\|(Object)\|message`, `Teamcenter.Import_ChildrenParent`, `MxGenAIConnector.IM_Collection_RetrieveNearestNeighbors`). Both executors resolved the root from the structure and had nowhere to put a selection | `mdl/executor/mapping_customhandler.go` (`resolveSchemaRoot`, `schemaRootClause`), `mdl/executor/cmd_import_mappings.go` + `cmd_export_mappings.go`, `mdl/grammar/MDLLexer.g4` (`ROOT`), `mdl/grammar/domains/MDLDomainModel.g4` | `root a/b/c` on the source clause, in member names. **The path may pass through an array where a value reference may not**: the mapping is then rooted at the array's ITEM (`root choices/message` → `(Object)\|choices\|(Object)\|message`), which is why this walks the index itself instead of reusing `resolvePath` — that one refuses an intermediate array because many items cannot collapse into one value (CE0256). Thread the selection through as the root's `parentPath` rather than adding a parameter: the isRoot branch already takes its lookup from there, so `""` keeps meaning "the structure's own root" and #248's fix is untouched. DESCRIBE **derives** the clause from the stored path rather than remembering it — drop the leading segment and every `(Object)`/`(Array)` marker, the inverse of how it resolves — so a Studio-Pro-authored mapping prints one too. The round-trip proof to aim for is `Unchanged import mapping …`: the rebuild is semantically equal and ADR-0008 elides the write entirely. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-267-nested-schema-root.mdl`, tests `mdl/executor/mapping_schema_root_test.go`. Issue ako/mxcli#267 |
